cases.body:
The House has reconvened and is now taking the following votes:

  1. Motion on Ordering the Previous Question (H.Res. 1174) – Democrats are urged to vote no on the Previous Question. Voting no will allow House Democrats to offer an amendment to the Rule that would call up the bipartisan Senate-passed bill to fund the Department of Homeland Security for FY26 except for ICE and CBP – VOTE NO – 15 minutes
  2. H.Res. 1174 – Rule providing for consideration of H.R. 6409 – FENCES Act; H.R. 6398 – RED Tape Act; H.Res. 1156 – Expressing support for tax policies that support working families; and H.R. 6387 – FIRE Act – VOTE NO – 5 minutes
  3. Democratic Motion to Discharge H.Res. 965 – Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 1689) to require the Secretary of Homeland Security to designate Haiti for temporary protected status (Rep. Pressley's Discharge Petition) (Rep. Pressley – Rules) – VOTE YES – 5 minutes

Following the first vote series, if the Democratic Motion to Discharge is adopted, the House will begin one hour of debate on H.Res. 965 – Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 1689) to require the Secretary of Homeland Security to designate Haiti for temporary protected status (Rep. Pressley's Discharge Petition).

After debate on H.Res. 965, the House will begin one hour of debate on H.R. 6409 – FENCES Act.

Following debate on H.R. 6409, the House will begin one hour of debate on H.R. 6398 – RED Tape Act.

After debate on H.R. 6398, the House will begin one hour of debate on H.Res. 1156 – Expressing support for tax policies that support working families.

Following debate on H.Res. 1156, the House will recess.

At approximately 9:15 p.m., the House will reconvene and take a second series of votes. These will be the last expected votes of the day.

Next/Last expected votes predicted: at approximately 9:15 p.m., on the motion to recommit and passage of H.R. 6409 and adoption of H.Res. 1156.

**Members are advised that legislative action related to FISA is still possible on the Floor today. Additional information will be provided as soon as it becomes available.

The House has reconvened and is now taking the following votes:

  1. Motion on Ordering the Previous Question (H.Res. 1275) – Democrats are urged to vote no on the Previous Question. Voting no will allow House Democrats to offer an amendment to the Rule that would call up Rep. Ross' No Rewards for January 6 Rioters Act, which prohibits the use of federal funds to compensate anyone prosecuted for the insurrection at the Capitol on January 6, 2021– VOTE NO – 15 minutes
  2. H.Res. 1275 – Rule providing for consideration of H.Con.Res. 96 – Expressing support for law enforcement officers; H.R. 5625 – Cashless Bail Reporting Act; H.R. 6260 – Keeping Violent Offenders Off Our Streets Act; H.R. 8365 – Monitor Accountability Act; and H.R. 8469 – Military Construction, Veterans Affairs, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2027 – VOTE NO – 5 minutes
  3. Motion on Ordering the Previous Question (H.Res. 1274) – Democrats are urged to vote no on the Previous Question. Voting no will allow House Democrats to offer an amendment to the Rule that would call up Rep. McDonald Rivet's Lower Prices at the Pump Act, which protects Americans from gasoline and fuel price gouging as President Trump's war of choice with Iran continues – VOTE NO – 5 minutes
  4. H.Res. 1274 – Rule providing that section 11 of House Resolution 1224 shall have no force or effect (decoupling H.R. 1346 – Nationwide Consumer and Fuel Retailer Choice Act of 2025 from H.R. 7567 – Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) – VOTE NO – 5 minutes

    Following these votes, the House will take the following vote on a bill considered under suspension of the Rules: 
     
  5. H.Res. 1252 – Resolution memorializing law enforcement officers killed in the line of duty (Rep. Guest – Judiciary) – 5 minutes

Following the first vote series, the House will begin one hour of debate on H.R. 1346 – Nationwide Consumer and Fuel Retailer Choice Act of 2025.

After debate on H.R. 1346, the House will begin one hour of debate on H.Con.Res. 96 – Expressing support for law enforcement officers.

At approximately 5:30 p.m., the House will take a second series of votes. These will be the last votes of the day.

Following last votes, the House will begin one hour of debate on H.Con.Res. 75 – Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove the United States Armed Forces from hostilities against the Islamic Republic of Iran.

Any recorded vote requested on H.Con.Res. 75 will be postponed until tomorrow.

Next/Last votes predicted: at approximately 5:30 p.m., on passage of H.R. 1346, adoption of H.Con.Res. 96, and two postponed Suspensions.

cases.body:
At approximately 3:30 p.m., the House will take the following votes on H.R. 8800 – National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027:

  1. Self #28 – Codifies protections and responsibilities for chaplains and subjects such protections to prosecution under the Uniform Code of Military Justice. This amendment is identical to H.R.8769, introduced by Rep. Keith Self in the 119th Congress – 15 minutes
  2. Issa #30 – Authorizes the Secretary to approve any eligible investor and cleared investment professional who meets the program’s statutory and regulatory requirements to assess potential investment opportunities that match with the Department of War's requirements or potential requirements. It also makes clear that the program is not capped, allowing an unlimited number of qualified investors, cleared personnel, and covered companies to participate at the discretion of the Secretary of War – 2 minutes
  3. Harrigan #44 – Prohibits use of automated speed enforcement cameras on military installations – 2 minutes
  4. Grothman #316 – Requires the Secretary of Defense to submit a report detailing options for reducing the number of civilians employed by the Department of Defense by 200,000 – 2 minutes
  5. Democratic Motion to Recommit on H.R. 8800 – VOTE YES – 5 minutes
  6. Final Passage of H.R. 8800 – National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (Rep. Rogers (AL) – Armed Services) – VOTE NO – 5 minutes

    Following these votes, the House will take the following votes:
     
  7. Democratic Motion to Recommit on H.R. 7008 – VOTE YES – 5 minutes
  8. Passage of H.R. 7008 – Stop Insider Trading Act (Rep. Steil – House Administration) – VOTE NO – 5 minutes
  9. Adoption of H.Con.Res. 113 – Establishing the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2027 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2028 through 2036 (Rep. Arrington – Budget) – VOTE NO – 5 minutes

These are the last votes for the day

After last votes, the House will begin one hour of debate on H.Con.Res. 89 – Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.

Any recorded vote requested on H.Con.Res. 89 will be postponed.

**Members are advised that the text of S. 1383 – SAVE America Act will be added to the NDAA upon passage of the NDAA on the Floor.

The House is currently in recess subject to the call of the Chair.

At approximately 1:25 p.m., the House will reconvene and take the following vote on a bill considered under suspension of the Rules: 

  1. Concurring in the Senate Amendment to H.R. 6500 – Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (Rep. Smith (MO) – Appropriations) – 15 minutes

    Following this vote, the House will take the following votes:
     
  2. Motion on Ordering the Previous Question (H.Res. 1499) – Democrats are urged to vote no on the Previous Question. Voting no will allow House Democrats to offer an amendment to the Rule that would call up Rep. Salinas' Universal Right To Vote by Mail Act, which helps ensure all eligible voters have the option to vote by mail in federal elections – VOTE NO – 5 minutes

Following the first vote series, the House will begin one hour of debate on H.Res. 1498 – Censuring Representative Chuck Edwards. Text can be found HERE.

After debate on H.Res. 1498, the House will begin debate on the two remaining bills listed for consideration under suspension of the Rules.

Following debate on Suspensions, the House will begin one hour of debate on H.R. 9436 – Northeast Lobsterman Protection Act of 2026.

After debate on H.R. 9436, the House will begin one hour of debate on H.Res. 1490 – Providing for the condemnation and denouncement of socialism in all its forms.

At approximately 5:15 p.m., the House will take a second series of votes. These will be the last votes of the day.

Next/Last votes predicted: at approximately 5:15 p.m., on adoption of H.Res. 1490, the motion to recommit and passage of H.R. 9436, and adoption of H.Res. 1498.

The House is now taking the following votes:

  1. Adoption of H.Res. 1490 – Providing for the condemnation and denouncement of socialism in all its forms (Rep. Crank – House Administration) – 15 minutes 
  2. Democratic Motion to Recommit on H.R. 9436 – VOTE YES – 5 minutes
  3. Passage of H.R. 9436 – Northeast Lobsterman Protection Act of 2026 (Rep. Lawler – Natural Resources) – VOTE NO – 5 minutes 
  4. Adoption of H.Res. 1498 – Censuring Representative Chuck Edwards (Rep. Guest – Ethics) – 5 minutes 

These are the last votes for the day

  1. Passage of H.J.Res. 1 – Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to require that the Supreme Court of the United States be composed of nine justices (Rep. Biggs (AZ) – Judiciary) – VOTE NO – 15 minutes

    Following this vote, the House will take the following vote:
     
  2. Passage of H.R. 1501 – Protecting Domestic Mining Act (Rep. Shreve – Natural Resources) – 5 minutes
